source.title: Locus Coeruleus Phasic, But Not Tonic, Activation Initiates Global Remapping in a Familiar Environment

confidence_rationale: The paper title and framing ('global remapping', 'network reset') sound directly on-topic for a decision-time attractor claim, and this is exactly why it is important: on close reading, the remapping is inferred entirely from immediate-early-gene expression compared across two 5-minute exposures separated by 20 minutes, not from any within-exploration/real-time readout. The authors themselves state their method cannot detect whether a population-code switch happens within seconds during ongoing exploration. This directly weakens the assumption that 'global remapping' literature licenses a decision-time attractor-width metric.
failure_signatures: Remapping is detected via catFISH immediate-early-gene (Arc/Zif268) compartmentalization comparing TWO separated 5-minute exposures 20 minutes apart, not via real-time recording during a single exploration bout

Authors explicitly state: 'rate remapping, place field rotation, or place field splitting occurring with novelty would not be detected as a loss of network overlap' -- their own technique cannot resolve within-session dynamics

The manipulation is pharmacological (glutamate microinfusion into LC) delivered over a 30-second infusion period, itself far longer than a single decision, with a further 60-second dwell before behavior begins
No optogenetic or electrophysiological demonstration exists in this paper of a remapping event occurring within seconds of phasic LC firing during ongoing behavior

mapping.source_claim_statement: Bilateral pharmacological activation of LC (glutamate microinfusion, mimicking phasic mode) prior to a rat's second exposure to an already-familiar environment causes the hippocampal population code -- indexed via catFISH IEG expression compared across the first and second 5-minute exposures -- to shift toward a 'novel-like' pattern (global remapping), whereas tonic-mode LC activators (bethanechol, orexin A, CRF) do not. LC silencing (clonidine) before a genuinely novel environment blocks the normal remapping that would otherwise occur.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the paper whose vocabulary ('global remapping', building on Bouret & Sara's 'network reset' theory) most closely resembles MECH-075's dorsal-leg prediction that high-LC-arousal widens/reorganizes the hippocampal attractor. But the paper's own methodology only ever compares population state ACROSS two temporally separated exposures (20 min apart) -- it provides no evidence about whether such a reorganization happens within the span of a single ongoing decision, which is exactly what V3-EXQ-905a's basin_width metric requires. If the field's best 'remapping' paper cannot demonstrate within-session dynamics, that is direct evidence the current literature does not support treating basin_width-within-a-decision as construct-valid for this mechanism.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Absence of a within-session demonstration in this paper is not proof that within-session remapping does not occur -- catFISH is fundamentally an across-exposure comparison technique and could not have detected a fast effect even if one existed. The authors' own limitations paragraph makes this explicit. Species (rat) and pharmacological (not optogenetic) manipulation also differ from V3's mechanistic framing.
mapping.source_context: Rat, open-field exploration, pharmacological LC microinfusion (glutamate/bethanechol/orexin-A/CRF/clonidine), catFISH immediate-early-gene compartmental analysis across dentate gyrus, CA1, and CA3.

confidence_components.notes: Solid, peer-reviewed J Neurosci study building on the well-established network-reset theoretical tradition (Bouret & Sara 2005). Mapping fidelity moderate: the conceptual link (LC phasic activation -> hippocampal population-code reorganization) is exactly the right shape for MECH-075's dorsal leg, but the methodology's inherent across-exposure blindness to within-session dynamics is a real limitation the authors themselves flag, not an artifact of REE's reading.
